title: The Curve y = sqrt(x^2 + 1) as Half of a Hyperbola
originalTopic: Recognizing a radical graph as a hyperbola branch
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graph of y = sqrt(x^2 + 1) looks like a flattened U with no lowest turning point visible in a tall window. Identify which familiar curve it belongs to, and state its domain, range, and symmetry.
finalAnswer: y^2 - x^2 = 1 \ (y > 0): \text{upper branch of a rectangular hyperbola; domain } \mathbb{R}, \text{ range } [1, \infty)

steps.title: Square to reveal the hidden equation
steps.mathExpression: y = \sqrt{x^2 + 1} \ \Rightarrow \ y^2 = x^2 + 1 \ \Rightarrow \ y^2 - x^2 = 1, \quad y \ge 1
steps.explanation: Squaring shows the graph sits on the hyperbola with vertices (0, plus or minus 1) and asymptotes y = plus or minus x, and only the upper branch survives because a square root is nonnegative.
steps.why: Squaring introduces an extra branch, so the sign restriction must be carried along to keep the graph correct.

steps.title: Use symmetry and the minimum
steps.explanation: The function is even, so the plot mirrors across the y-axis; the derivative is negative for x < 0, zero at x = 0 and positive for x > 0, giving the absolute minimum value 1.
steps.why: Even symmetry plus a single critical point explains the smooth rounded bottom at (0, 1) that a coarse window flattens into a straight line.

steps.title: Describe the end behavior
steps.explanation: The curve approaches the lines y = x (right side) and y = -x (left side) ever more closely, staying just above them.
steps.why: Rationalizing the difference quantifies how tightly the branch hugs its slant asymptotes, which is what makes wide windows look deceptively linear.

steps.title: Pick a window that shows the curvature
steps.explanation: This frame includes the vertex (0, 1), a little of the empty region below it to make the minimum obvious, and enough width for the arms to appear nearly straight as they approach the asymptotes.
steps.why: A y-range starting at 0 rather than at 1 is what reveals the gap between the curve and its asymptotes.
